posts.title: Are you really 90% bacteria? Not even close 🦠
posts.text:
You've heard bacteria outnumber you 10 to 1. They don't 🦠

Follow for more of your body, counted.
#humanbody #microbiome #bacteria #science #facts
posts.text_youtube:
The famous '10 bacteria for every human cell' claim is wrong.

• ~38 trillion bacteria vs ~30 trillion human cells — roughly 1:1, not 10:1
• All your bacteria together weigh about 0.2 kg (~200 g)
• About 25 trillion of your ~30 trillion human cells are red blood cells, which have no nucleus

Source: Sender, Fuchs & Milo (2016), PLoS Biology — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4991899/

posts.title: 2 meters of DNA in every cell 🧬
posts.text:
There are 2 meters of thread inside almost every cell you have 🧬

Follow for more of your body, counted.
#dna #humanbody #science #biology #facts
posts.text_youtube:
Almost every cell in your body holds about 2 meters of DNA.

• ~2 m of DNA per cell, packed into a nucleus ~10 µm wide
• 2 m ÷ 10 µm = ~200,000× longer than its container
• Same ratio: a basketball (24 cm) would hold 48 km of thread
• ~3 billion base pairs from each parent, ~6 billion per cell
• (Mature red blood cells have no nucleus, hence 'almost')

Sources: BioNumbers (Harvard) #104208 and #108957 — https://bionumbers.hms.harvard.edu/bionumber.aspx?id=104208 · https://bionumbers.hms.harvard.edu/bionumber.aspx?id=108957

posts.title: Most of your eye can't see color 👁️
posts.text:
How much of your eye actually sees color? Most people get this wrong 👁️

Follow for more of your body, counted.
#eyes #vision #humanbody #science #facts
posts.text_youtube:
Your retina has two kinds of light sensors.

• Rods (~95% of photoreceptors): light and dark only, no color
• Cones (~5%, about 6–7 million per eye): color
• The fovea, the center of your vision, contains only cones and no rods

Source: StatPearls, 'Neuroanatomy, Retina' (NCBI Bookshelf) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK545310/

posts.title: Your blood vessels could circle Earth 2.4 times 🌍
posts.text:
Your blood vessels laid end to end — how far would they go? 🩸

Follow for more of your body, counted.
#heart #bloodvessels #humanbody #science #facts
posts.text_youtube:
Laid end to end, your blood vessels would stretch over 60,000 miles.

• 60,000 miles ≈ 96,000 km
• Earth's circumference ≈ 40,075 km → almost 2.5 times around
• Most vessels are tiny: capillaries, venules and arterioles
• All of it is powered by one fist-sized pump

Sources: Cleveland Clinic — https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/17059-how-does-blood-flow-through-your-body · https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/21640-blood-vessels

posts.title: You lose 100 hairs a day — and that's normal 💇
posts.text:
You lose up to 100 hairs every day. So why aren't you bald? 💇

Follow for more of your body, counted.
#hair #humanbody #science #facts #biology
posts.text_youtube:
Losing hair every day is normal.

• 50–100 hairs a day is normal (American Academy of Dermatology)
• That's up to ~36,500 a year (100 × 365)
• Your scalp has 100,000+ hairs: ~110,000 for brunettes, closer to ~150,000 for blondes
• Your body has about 5 million hair follicles

Sources: AAD — https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/hair-loss/causes/fall-out · Cleveland Clinic — https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/body-hair

posts.title: The '7-year new body' myth, in numbers ⏳
posts.text:
Every 7 years you become a new person? You don't ⏳

Follow for more of your body, counted.
#humanbody #myths #science #facts #biology
posts.text_youtube:
Your body doesn't reset on a 7-year clock — each part runs on its own.

• ~330 billion cells are replaced every day; close to 90% are blood cells
• Your gut lining is replaced every few days
• Most of the adult skeleton is replaced about every 10 years, through lifelong remodeling

Sources: Sender & Milo (2021), Nature Medicine — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-020-01182-9 · Weizmann Institute — https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/node/11205 · U.S. Surgeon General, Bone Health report — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK45504/

posts.title: Your nerves are faster than a race car ⚡
posts.text:
Some of your nerve signals are faster than a race car. Others walk ⚡

Follow for more of your body, counted.
#nerves #brain #humanbody #science #facts
posts.text_youtube:
Your nerves have a fast lane and a slow lane.

• Large myelinated fibers (A-alpha): up to 120 m/s ≈ 430 km/h
• Some unmyelinated pain fibers (C): about 0.5–2.5 m/s
• Myelin, a fatty insulation, is what makes the fast lane fast — that's why the ache after a stubbed toe arrives late

Source: J.A. Kiernan, 'Nerve fibre types', University of Western Ontario — https://publish.uwo.ca/~jkiernan/fibrtyp.htm
